title: `sys_oauth_application.client_secret`'s "hashed/encrypted at rest" description asserts a protection without citing what enforces it — the measurement has now been paid for twice
body:
Filed by the `domain:identity` execution seat as the cross-lane remainder of **#8011**. It lands in `packages/platform-objects` (`domain:metadata`'s package), so it is filed separately and **unassigned/unlabeled for triage** rather than absorbed. Comment-only change, zero behavioural surface.

## Background — the claim is TRUE, and that is exactly why this is worth doing

#8011 verified by real round-trip that both credential columns are genuinely hashed at rest. Measured, not inferred:

| column | declares | what actually lands | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `sys_scim_provider.scim_token` | label `"(hash)"` | SHA-256/base64url of the inner base token | **claim holds** |
| `sys_oauth_application.client_secret` | "hashed/encrypted at rest" | SHA-256/base64url of the plaintext | **claim holds** |

Neither column ever receives cleartext.

## The problem this card fixes

The declarations **assert** the protection without citing what enforces it. A declaration-reading survey therefore cannot confirm them from the storage side — both are plain `Field.text`, neither carries `internal: true`, and both are API-reachable (`sys_oauth_application`: `['get','list']`). So the survey correctly records them as *unverified rather than clean*, and someone re-measures.

**That has now happened twice** — the #7902 survey, then #8011 — on a claim that was true both times. The citation is what stops a third.

`sys_scim_provider` (②-c) **needs nothing**: `sys-scim-provider.object.ts:16-20` already cites `storeSCIMToken: 'hashed'` in the object docstring and the field description already says "Hashed bearer credential". That is precisely why the survey scored it near-closed while ②-d stayed open. Only `client_secret` lacks the pointer.

## Suggested shape (not decided here)

One-line description change on `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-oauth-application.object.ts:304`, wording proposed by the dev that measured it:

> OAuth client secret — stored as a SHA-256 digest, never plaintext (`@better-auth/oauth-provider` `storeClientSecret`, which defaults to hashed whenever the jwt plugin is enabled; wired in `plugin-auth` `auth-manager.ts:2473`). Shown once at registration.

Supporting evidence, read off `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.0-rc.2` dist rather than docs: `storeClientSecret` (`dist/resource-challenge-2qgK1B-a.mjs:455`) has **no cleartext branch at all** — every path hashes, encrypts, or throws. The repo sets neither `storeClientSecret` nor `disableJwtPlugin` anywhere in `packages/`, and `auth-manager.ts:2473` registers the jwt plugin, so the default resolves to `"hashed"`. The plaintext is spliced into the *response* only (`dist/index.mjs:3560` persists the digest, `:3595` returns the plaintext).

## ⚠️ Carry this forward — #8011's acceptance bar misfires as literally worded

#8011 stated the bar as "a round-trip that reproduces the stored value from the plaintext proves it is **not** hashed". Read literally that is backwards: unsalted SHA-256 **is** reproducible from the plaintext by construction — that is how every hash verifier works, better-auth's own included — so the literal sentence would score every correctly-hashed credential in the repo as unhashed, `sys_api_key.key` (#7728) included, and manufacture a false P1 on a clean surface.

The discriminator that was actually applied: whether the stored value **equals** the plaintext or is **reversible** to it. Neither holds — the only inverse better-auth has is recompute-and-compare (`verifyStoredClientSecret` / `verifySCIMToken` use `constantTimeEqual` on a re-derived digest, never a decrypt).

Recorded here because a later audit mechanically applying that sentence would fabricate a finding on a surface that is correct.

Also worth carrying: these are 32-char machine-generated secrets, not user passwords, so an unsalted fast digest is the standard construction — the absence of bcrypt/argon2 is **not** a finding.

## ⚠️ The trap a naive pin falls into

For `scim_token` the bearer returned to the IdP admin is `base64url("BASE:providerId:organizationId")`, but the stored digest covers **`BASE` alone**. Hashing the returned bearer yields a value that does **not** match the stored digest. An audit that skipped the decode step would report a **false negative on a correct implementation**.

Parent: #8011. Related: #8192 (the regression pin for this posture, PR #8305), #7728, #7990, #7902.
